notes: Values are transcribed from type certificate data sheets (TCDS). Each entry names the citing document; a type without an entry gets no rated-limit finding. Types certified in experimental, restricted, or military categories have no civil sheet and are left out on purpose.

source is the sheet an entry's limits are cited from. Where the verification reads a figure from another sheet, speed_source names the sheet of the airspeed limits (Vmo, Mmo, and Vne) and altitude_source the sheet of the maximum operating altitude; each limit is cited from its own sheet.

verification says how each value was read: easa-tcds-text means the figure was read from the cited EASA sheet's text on prepared_on; faa-tcds-number means it is transcribed from the named FAA sheet without a fetched copy. Where one designator covers several models or modification states, the entry carries the highest certified value among them, so a reading must exceed every variant's limit before it counts.

max_operating_altitude_ft is the certified maximum operating altitude. vmo_kias and mmo are the maximum operating limit speeds; vne_kias is the never-exceed speed of types certified with one. null means the sheet states no such limit or it was not transcribed.

Each limit is one value. Where a sheet gives Vmo as an altitude schedule, the entry carries the highest applicable value, so no reading is compared with a limit stricter than any the sheet states; a comparison may therefore understate an exceedance at the altitudes with a lower limit, never overstate one.

A finding compares sustained readings with these limits through the ISA atmosphere and, for speed, an estimated or reported true airspeed. It describes received data; it never establishes a violation, an emergency, or a cause.
